summary.text: Addison McDowell is the Republican incumbent seeking re-election in North Carolina's 6th Congressional District.
A former congressional staffer and Blue Cross Blue Shield lobbyist, he was first elected in 2024 and took office in January 2025 as one of the youngest members of Congress.
His office says his top priorities are addressing the drug crisis and border security.

paragraphs.text: McDowell was born in 1994; Ballotpedia lists Whiteville, North Carolina as his birthplace, and his House biography describes him as a native of Lexington, North Carolina.
He earned a bachelor's degree in political science and government from the University of North Carolina at Charlotte.
In 2016, while he was in college, his younger brother Luke died after taking a pill laced with fentanyl, and McDowell has said that loss motivated him to seek office.
McDowell worked on staff for Reps. Richard Hudson and Ted Budd (now a U.S. Senator), helping constituents, according to his House biography, and later worked as a lobbyist for Blue Cross Blue Shield.
He won a crowded 2024 Republican primary for the open seat after endorsement by Donald Trump, then won the November 2024 general election; it was his first elected position.
He succeeded Democrat Kathy Manning, who did not seek re-election after the district was redrawn.
In Congress, McDowell serves on the Transportation and Infrastructure, Natural Resources, and Budget committees.
He advanced to the 2026 general election after the Republican primary was canceled.
He lives in Davie County with his wife, Rachel, and their two daughters, according to his House biography.

sources.title: The personal story this lawmaker says brought him to Congress
